key_insight: ZeroMAG can generate task- and subject-conditioned multimodal adapters from unlabeled target EEG recordings, enabling plug-and-play extension of frozen EEG foundation models without target labels or target-side fine-tuning.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path to deploy pretrained EEG models on heterogeneous real-world recordings that include extra physiological channels, while preserving the original model and avoiding costly supervised retraining.
method: Builds a configuration-invariant adapter that standardizes how companion modalities are attached to a frozen EEG encoder and prediction head.
Uses unlabeled target recordings plus task context to form a modality-subject-task condition.
Generates adapter weights in a function-constrained latent space learned from source adapters.
evidence_signal: Across six held-out target datasets and three EEG foundation model backbones, ZeroMAG improves balanced accuracy by 7.22 points over EEG-only inference and 4.89 points over direct weight regression, reaching within 0.50 points of supervised multimodal adaptation on average.
watch_item: Performance depends on functional supervision during both representation learning and conditional generation, so adapter quality may drop if the source-adapter prior or target modality structure is weak.
paper_title: ZeroMAG: Zero-Shot Multimodal Adapter Generation for Plug-and-Play EEG Foundation Models
